page: Amazon Web Services r8i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor, delivering 192 virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The dedicated CPU allocation operates at a speed of 3.9 GHz, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1D cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks rank in the top tier. Single-core performance presents a relative tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the average tier, while Geekbench single-core and text processing fall into the strong tier.

From a resource-density perspective, the high allocation of DDR5 memory relative to the 192 vCPUs provides a consolidated footprint for large-scale deployments, reducing the need for multi-node clustering. However, the lack of local storage requires external storage provisioning, which may impact overall infrastructure design. The processor supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, contributing to top-tier prompt processing speeds for large language models, though text generation speeds remain in the strong to average tiers. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise database operations, and memory-bound scientific simulations.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server featuring 192 vCPUs and 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor on the Nitro hypervisor, it delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and memory bandwidth. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs, relying on a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. While single-core stress tests and text generation speeds represent relative performance tradeoffs in the average to strong tiers, its support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions enables top-tier prompt processing for large language models. This configuration is designed for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases and enterprise data processing.
